messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Meze sur la vojo de nia vivo mi trovis min en malluma arbaro, ĉar la prava vojo estis perdita.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|--------| | **Nel** | preposition + definite article “in the” | **Meze** | “midway” | **WRONG** (semantic mismatch) | | **mezzo** | noun “midpoint, middle” | **sur** | “on / upon” | **WRONG** | | **del** | preposition + article “of the” | **de** | “of” | OK | | **cammin** | noun “road, journey” | **vojo** | “road / way” | OK | | **di** | preposition linking “cammin” to “nostra vita” | **de** | “of” | OK | | **nostra** | possessive adjective “our” | **nia** | “our” | OK | | **vita** | noun “life” | **vivo** | “life” | OK | | **mi** | reflexive pronoun (1st sg.) “myself / I” | **mi** | “I” | OK | | **ritrovai** | verb “found (myself)” | **trovis** | “found” | OK | | **per** | preposition “within, through” | **en** | “in” | OK | | **una** | indefinite article “a / an” | *(none)* | — | **MISSING** | | **selva** | noun “forest, wood” | **arbaro** | “forest” | OK | | **oscura** | adjective “dark” | **malluma** | “dark” | OK | | **ché** | conjunction “for, because” (causal) | **ĉar** | “because” | OK | | **la** | definite article “the” | **la** | “the” | OK | | **diritta** | adjective “right, straight” | **prava** | “right / correct” | OK | | **via** | noun “way, road” | **vojo** | “way / road” | OK | | **era** | verb “was, had been” (imperfect) | **estis** | “was” | OK | | **smarrita** | past participle “lost, missed” | **perdita** | “lost / missed” | OK |

### Items to Review
- **WRONG:** - *Nel* → *Meze* (should convey “in the”, not “midway”). - *mezzo* → *sur* (should convey “midpoint”, not “on”).
- **MISSING:** - *una* (indefinite article) has no direct equivalent in Esperanto; the translation omitted it.
All other mappings are correct and show proper grammatical agreement in Esperanto.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
